- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots in subsequent days — reduce forecast peak magnitude by 5–10% to reflect mean reversion.
- If model forecast is significantly below recent historical mean (last 5–10 days), and sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, increase forecast to align with momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period price increases — add 2–5% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is positive or neutral.
- If sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., >0.30 for 3+ consecutive days), model often fails to capture rally — increase forecast by 3–7% in early-to-mid horizon to reflect sentiment-driven acceleration.
- Model tends to lag sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns positive after 3–5 days, adjust forecast to rise 1–3 days ahead of sentiment change, not wait for confirmation.
